newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate likely to ratify NATO expansion - Lott.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate likely to ratify NATO expansion - Lott.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said on Wednesday the prospects were good for Senate ratification of NATO expansion.

The Mississippi Republican, on a visit to Brussels, said in a statement released in Washington: "I believe the prospects for Senate ratification are good, but we should recognise that the opponents of NATO enlargement are organised and they are making their case."
Lott's comments came ahead of next week's North Atlantic Treaty Organisation summit in Madrid at which Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be invited to join.
The 100-seat U.S. Senate will have to ratify any decision to expand NATO with a two-thirds majority.
The Clinton administration, which strongly backs bringing in new members, has launched a political intiative to ensure it wins that backing despite vocal resistance from some conservative Senators.
A Senate delegation met with NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana and the 16 NATO ambassadors in Brussels, Lott said.
"I believe that NATO's next round of enlargement should not be its last. We discussed the importance of keeping the door to NATO open after Madrid," Lott said.
"I believe we must ensure Russia's voice in NATO does not turn into a veto," he said. "There is concern that the agreement with Russia could lead to a weakening of NATO," he added.
Russia signed a new partnership deal with NATO on May 27 which gives Moscow a say in some alliance security matters.
Lott said the Senate in its ratification process would consider several issues including overall costs, how costs would be shared, and the relationship with Russia.
